claims.statement: The web package (@open-inspect/web) is a framework-free BFF: it signs every server-to-control-plane request with its own SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET on the service:web sig1 channel, forwards only Better Auth's opaque session cookie, and holds no OAuth provider credentials or admission policy — the enabled sign-in provider set is resolved from the control plane at request time for /login.

src/app/api/auth/[...auth]/route.ts aliases both GET and POST to proxyBrowserAuthRequest, which forwards only the six allowlisted method+path pairs declared in the shared BROWSER_AUTH_PROXY_ROUTES (sign-in/social, GitHub and Google callbacks, get-session, sign-out, error) and returns 404 for anything else before dispatching.

The browser-auth proxy sanitizes the forward: it copies only Accept, Accept-Language, Content-Type, Cookie, Origin, and User-Agent; takes the client IP solely from the platform-trusted header (X-Vercel-Forwarded-For on Vercel, CF-Connecting-IP on Cloudflare) and forwards it as X-OpenInspect-Client-IP; strips hop-by-hop and content-encoding/content-length response headers while preserving every Set-Cookie; forces Cache-Control: no-store; and dispatches with redirect: manual and cache: no-store.

getServerAuthSession is the server-side authentication seam for BFF routes: it serializes only the opaque Better Auth session cookie (serializeBrowserSessionCookies matches (__Secure-)openinspect.session_token(.N) names, rejects duplicate or malformed values, and returns null when absent), dispatches GET /api/auth/get-session through the checked auth proxy, maps 401 to null, validates the payload with browserAuthSessionResponseSchema (canonical user id and session.userId === user.id), and wraps transport failures in AuthenticationUnavailableError.

useAuthSession is the client-side auth seam — an SWR subscription to /api/auth/get-session via browserApiFetch exposing loading/authenticated/unauthenticated/unavailable — and AppAuthBoundary wraps the whole (app) route group, rendering a spinner, an unavailable page, a sign-in pitch, or the children accordingly; signIn refuses to navigate to non-HTTPS redirect URLs.

The auth boundary is pinned by ESLint config and tests: packages/web/src bans next-auth imports and any lib/auth path, and bans the global fetch everywhere except the two app-owned seams lib/browser-api-fetch.ts (browser-to-BFF, /api/* path type, same-origin mode/credentials) and lib/control-plane-transport.ts (BFF-to-control-plane dispatch); client-auth-boundary-eslint.test.ts and server-auth-boundary-eslint.test.ts execute the real ESLint flat config against representative sources to keep the pins honest.

controlPlaneUserFetch is the user-authenticated control-plane entrypoint: it serializes the session cookie from next/headers (responding 401 without dispatching when absent), defaults Content-Type to application/json, attaches middleware-derived trace/request correlation, and delegates transport and signing to the layers below it.

dispatchWebServiceRequest is the signing boundary: it deletes caller-supplied Authorization, actor, service, and signature headers so only credentials minted at this boundary identify a web-service request, requires SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET, and applies sig1 headers binding method, exact URL, and body hash — callers build the URL once, so the signed URL is always the dispatched URL.

dispatchControlPlaneFetch routes through the Cloudflare CONTROL_PLANE_WORKER service binding to avoid same-account worker-to-worker fetch restrictions (error 1042), falls back to URL-based fetch on Vercel and unconditionally in development (the OpenNext dev binding is a failing stub), and bounds every request with a 15-second AbortSignal.timeout merged with any caller signal.

settingsProxy generates authenticated GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE BFF handlers that check the serialized session cookie before reading a mutation body, cap mutation bodies at 4 MiB (413 beyond), forward the client's If-Match header unchanged as an opaque CAS revision token, and relay responses as JSON with Cache-Control: private, no-store plus etag, retry-after, and x-request-id.

Query and path-parameter forwarding are allowlisted: buildControlPlanePath forwards only declared parameter names to the control plane, and providerAccountSettingsProxy wraps settingsProxy with pattern validation of provider-account ids and subscription provider names before a request is built.

The API routes under src/app/api proxy the control-plane surface the UI needs — sessions (list/create, inbox, prompt, ws-token, title, read-state, children, archive, attachments, diffs, media, participant profiles, sandbox access, skills), repos plus global/repo/environment secrets, environments and their image triggers, the unified image-builds feed, automations with pause/resume/trigger/runs, model-provider accounts with enable/disable/reconnect/verify and device authorizations, skills and skill-profiles, mcp-servers, scm-settings, commit-signing, keyboard-shortcuts, integration settings, Slack channel listing, model preferences, and four analytics GETs.

Authorization placement varies deliberately across BFF routes: list routes such as GET /api/sessions and the inbox forward without a local session check (the control plane authenticates the forwarded cookie), while mutation routes pre-check getServerAuthSession or the session cookie so an unauthenticated request body is never read; POST bodies for sessions and automations are field-allowlisted, with co-located tests using a hostile-identity fixture to assert forged identity and token fields never reach the control plane.

POST /api/sessions/[id]/prompt re-validates the request against the shared zod prompt schema (blank prompts rejected, attachment shape checked) and stamps source: web before proxying; POST /api/sessions/[id]/ws-token verifies the Better Auth session and then proxies to the control plane to mint the WebSocket token the browser uses to subscribe.

GET /api/sessions/[id]/media/[artifactId] validates both path ids against strict alphanumeric patterns, forwards the client's Range header, and streams the control-plane media response with Cache-Control: private, no-store and Vary: Cookie; image-build routes answer 501 with a shared provider-derived message when the deployment's sandbox provider lacks image support.

A Next.js middleware matching /api/:path* stamps correlation headers — passing through a valid x-trace-id (otherwise generating a fresh UUID) and always generating a fresh 8-character x-request-id — onto both the downstream request and the response.

useSessionTransport owns the socket mechanics only: it fetches a token from /api/sessions/{id}/ws-token (a 401 surfaces as a sign-in authError), opens NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL/sessions/{id}/ws, sends a subscribe message with token and clientId on open, pings every 30 seconds, and hands schema-validated messages to onMessage without interpreting protocol semantics.

The transport's close policy, decided by the pure closeDirective function, is: 4001 auth-required sets authError and clears the token without retry; 4002 session-expired sets a connectionError and clears the token; an unclean close or 4004 invalid-message retries with exponential backoff (1s base, 30s cap) up to 5 attempts then gives up with a surfaced connectionError; a clean close does not retry; and markHealthy — called by useSessionSocket once the reducer reports ready — resets the backoff counter.

The transport is race-safe via a monotonic connect epoch: reconnect() and unmount invalidate any connect() still awaiting its token so an abandoned attempt can never open a socket alongside its replacement, and reconnect() drops the token, socket, and pending retry timer before starting fresh.

sessionSocketReducer is a pure projection from normalized actions (server_message, events_appended, history_requested, socket_closed) to SessionSocketState; the WebSocket client, token buffering, and SWR cache effects all live outside it, and useSessionSocket seeds it from the server-fetched snapshot via createSessionSocketState.

A subscribed message is an authoritative resync: the reducer replaces local artifacts and events with the snapshot rather than merging (reconnects must clear stale client data) and resets loadingHistory so a fetch_history dropped by a disconnect cannot block loadOlderEvents; socket_closed clears ready, presenceSynced, and the participant list.

Sandbox failure state is provider-reported, not a status label: sandbox_error stores the control plane's own message in sandboxError and clears runtime access URLs; warming, spawning, and ready clear sandboxError because a new attempt supersedes the last failure; sandbox_status spawning/stale/stopped/failed clear the code-server/VNC/ttyd/tunnel access state, and a replacement spawn also clears the sandbox dashboard URL.

Artifacts upsert by id (creates prepend, updates replace in place so ordering stays stable); session_branch updates follow an explicit multi-repo attribution rule — no hydrated member list updates the scalar branch only, exactly one member updates that member and mirrors the scalar, and with multiple members an unscoped or unknown-member update is ignored rather than attributed to the primary while the scalar mirrors only when the named member is primary; positive finite step_finish costs accrue to totalCost.

history_page prepends its page and carries the new cursor and hasMore, while a rejected fetch_history (an error message) resets loadingHistory; loadOlderEvents only fires when hasMoreHistory is true, loading is not already in progress, and a cursor exists, requesting pages of 200 events.

Token events carry the full accumulated text for an assistant segment rather than deltas, so ingestLiveSandboxEvent buffers the pending text outside React state (a ref — high-frequency tokens must not re-render) and emits it exactly once, with the token's original timestamp, on the matching execution_complete or context_compacted; stopExecution flushes pending partial text before sending stop; collapseReplayTokenEvents compacts replayed history to one token per compaction-delimited segment regardless of storage ordering between token and completion events.

toUiArtifact maps the wire SessionArtifact to the UI Artifact by narrowing each loosely-typed metadata field to its expected type and deriving the PR display status — preferring the tracked lifecycleState/isDraft pair via the shared toDisplayStatus and falling back to the legacy state key for artifacts that predate PR lifecycle tracking.

swrKeysToRevalidate decides per message which SWR caches a socket message invalidates: PR artifacts, session titles, and status changes revalidate the unarchived session list and inbox; child_session_update additionally revalidates the children list; a terminal execution_complete revalidates the inbox; diff_state_changed revalidates the diff; subscribed refreshes diff, children, participant profiles, and inbox — and only PR artifacts revalidate the session list because high-frequency media artifacts cannot change it; useSessionSocket maps these keys through mutate and is the only place the hook touches the SWR cache.

Prompt sending is a correlated request: at most one prompt may await acknowledgement at a time, each request carries a clientRequestId and settles on the matching prompt_queued or prompt_cancelled, on a matching error, on disconnect (all pending requests fail), or on a 15-second ack timeout after at most a 5-second subscription wait; no optimistic user message is inserted because the server persists the user_message event and broadcasts it to every client including the sender.

Sandbox access credentials (code-server/VNC/ttyd) are fetched by a dedicated SWR hook keyed only while sandboxStatus is ready, cleared by useSessionSocket on spawning/error/status transitions and refreshed on subscribe or sandbox_access_changed, and merged into the returned sessionState.

The session route's layout is a server component that fetches the session snapshot with controlPlaneUserFetch (cache: no-store), redirects to /login on 401 and calls notFound() on 404, and publishes the validated snapshot via SessionSnapshotProvider so the client page can seed useSessionSocket with server data before the socket opens.

The dashboard is a new-session composer that warms a draft session as soon as the user starts typing or attaches a file (archiving superseded warm sessions in the background), and on submit reuses the warm session id, uploads attachments, sends the first prompt over HTTP POST /api/sessions/{id}/prompt rather than a WebSocket, mutates the session-list and inbox caches, and routes to /session/{id}.

The /settings page renders a category panel registry driven by the ?tab= query parameter (with a mobile list/detail pattern via history state) whose default category is secrets; the Images category only exists when supportsRepoImages() is true, which derives the deployment's sandbox provider from NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_PROVIDER (default modal, throwing on unknown values) and mirrors the control plane's image-capable provider list.

The timeline layer shapes reducer events for display: timeline-items filters to renderable events (hiding user messages still pending in the prompt queue), dedupes (tool calls by identity key, executions per message, superseded tokens), groups consecutive same-tool tool calls, nests subtask activity under its Task call, and collapses each completed user turn into a work_group while leaving in-flight and partial-history turns flat; timeline-virtual-rows builds virtual rows with per-kind size estimates that session-timeline renders through @tanstack/react-virtual with load-older and read-state wiring.

The web app deploys either to Vercel (the default web_platform) with CONTROL_PLANE_URL, the NEXT_PUBLIC_* set, and the sensitive SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET as project environment variables, or to Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext, where Terraform runs build:cloudflare with the NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables set at build time, generates a wrangler.production.toml declaring the CONTROL_PLANE_WORKER service binding and nodejs_compat/global_fetch_strictly_public, uploads SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET as a Worker secret after deploy, and optionally attaches a Cloudflare-managed custom domain.

NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables (including NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL, the address useSessionTransport dials) are inlined into the client bundle at build time, so changing them requires a rebuild/redeploy; server-only values such as SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET and CONTROL_PLANE_URL are read at runtime and are not subject to this constraint.

providers.tsx installs the global SWR configuration used across the app: a fetcher built on browserApiFetch, revalidateOnFocus, and a 2-second deduping interval, alongside the theme provider and toaster.
